claim: Giving Claude Code a runnable verification check (tests, build exit code, linter, or screenshot diff) closes the self-correction loop without human supervision, since without such a check 'looks done' is the only available stopping signal and every mistake waits for a human to notice it.
stance_target: rigid evals / zero-hallucination quality control for autonomous coding agents requires an executable verification signal, not reliance on the agent's own judgment of completion
scope_conditions: Claude Code official best practices, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: Claude stops when the work looks done. Without a check it can run, “looks done” is the only signal available, and you become the verification loop: every mistake waits for you to notice it. Give Claude something that produces a pass or fail, and the loop closes on its own.

claim: Claude Code offers four escalating levels of verification gating for an unattended agent run: a single-prompt check, a persistent /goal condition re-evaluated by a separate evaluator after every turn, a deterministic Stop hook script that blocks turn-end until the check passes, and a 'second opinion' verification subagent with a fresh model that tries to refute the implementing agent's own result.
stance_target: a probabilistic-sequence/rigid-eval architecture for an AI software factory should layer increasingly deterministic gates as autonomy and run duration increase
scope_conditions: Claude Code official best practices, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: As a deterministic gate: a Stop hook runs your check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes. ... By a second opinion: a verification subagent ... has a fresh model try to refute the result, so the agent doing the work isn't the one grading it.

claim: Claude Code's auto permission mode (default as of v2.1.283+, or on Pro/Max/Team plans on earlier versions) runs a separate classifier model that reviews most agent actions and blocks only actions that look risky -- scope escalation, unknown infrastructure, or hostile-content-driven actions -- allowing routine work to proceed without per-action human approval.
stance_target: a classifier-model-mediated permission layer is a viable mechanism for continuous, largely-unattended agent operation while still constraining blast radius
scope_conditions: Claude Code v2.1.283+, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: a separate classifier model reviews most actions instead of you and blocks only what looks risky, such as scope escalation, unknown infrastructure, or hostile-content-driven actions.

claim: An over-long CLAUDE.md (persistent project-context file) causes Claude to ignore roughly half of its own instructions because important rules get lost in the noise; the recommended fix is ruthless pruning, converting hard rules to deterministic hooks, and testing each line by asking whether removing it would cause mistakes.
stance_target: persistent context/convention files for coding agents have a practical information-density ceiling beyond which they become counterproductive, relevant to the context-ingestion pillar
scope_conditions: Claude Code CLAUDE.md usage guidance, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: The over-specified CLAUDE.md. If your CLAUDE.md is too long, Claude ignores half of it because important rules get lost in the noise. Fix: Ruthlessly prune. If Claude already does something correctly without the instruction, delete it or convert it to a hook.

claim: Claude Code supports unattended batch automation across thousands of files via a fan-out script pattern: looping `claude -p` over a generated file list with `--allowedTools` pre-approving the needed tools and `--permission-mode dontAsk` denying anything else, after first testing the prompt on 2-3 files.
stance_target: scripted fan-out with pre-approved tool allowlists is the documented pattern for scaling a single coding agent across a large migration or codebase-wide task, directly relevant to the continuous-operation/triggers pillar
scope_conditions: Claude Code CLI automation guidance, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: for file in $(cat files.txt); do claude -p "Migrate $file from Python 2 to Python 3. Return OK or FAIL." --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(git commit *)" --permission-mode dontAsk done ... Test on a few files, then run on all of them

claim: An adversarial code-review step -- a subagent reviewing a diff in a fresh context, seeing only the diff and stated acceptance criteria rather than the implementing agent's own reasoning -- becomes more important the longer an agent works unattended, because the independent reviewer evaluates the result on its own terms rather than inheriting the implementer's biases.
stance_target: adversarial model review (a separate review agent with independent context) is the recommended quality-control mechanism for autonomous coding agent output, matching the zero-hallucination pillar's adversarial-review requirement
scope_conditions: Claude Code official best practices, as of Oct 2026
quoted_support: The longer Claude works unattended, the more an independent check matters before you count the work as done. A reviewer running in a fresh subagent context sees only the diff and the criteria you give it, not the reasoning that produced the change, so it evaluates the result on its own terms.
